problem_statement: wrappixel/materialpro-react-lite (MaterialPro React Lite) is a runnable Vite + TypeScript + Material-UI admin dashboard. It ships a "Delivery focus" filter card rendered by the FullLayout shell so it follows the operator across every working surface of the console: the operations dashboard, the delivery tracker (/tables/basic-table) and the sample workspace page (/sample-page). The card reuses the app's OWN Basic Table delivery rows (Sunil Joshi · Elite Admin · $3.9k · Low, Andrew McDownland · Real Homes WP Theme · $24.5k · Medium, Christopher Jamil · MedicalPro WP Theme · $12.8k · High, Nirav Joshi · Hosting Press HTML · $2.4k · Critical): a priority chip row (All / Low / Medium / High / Critical) filters a card grid of those rows, with a live readout inside the card ("Showing N of M · <Priority>"). In the current state the card is broken in four independent ways that must be repaired together: (1) the chip row and card grid are pinned to a fixed-width, no-wrap track, so on a 390px mobile viewport the whole document overflows horizontally and the dashboard gets a horizontal scrollbar; (2) the chips and cards are rendered as flat, borderless grey blocks instead of the rounded pale-blue MaterialPro chip/card treatment, an obvious visual regression against the design language; (3) the card is mounted only on the dashboard route, so the delivery tracker and sample workspace surfaces are missing the filter card entirely; and (4) clicking a priority chip re-filters the grid but the readout is bound to a value captured once at mount, so it stays frozen on "Showing 4 of 4 · All" even though the grid has filtered. Repair the card so its chips and grid reflow within any viewport with no horizontal overflow at 390px, are restyled back to the rounded pale-blue MaterialPro treatment, are present on the dashboard, tracker and workspace surfaces, and so the readout live-reflects the active priority and filtered count after a chip is clicked. Keep the shell, charts, cards, tables, routes, and local assets intact.
required_content: The Delivery focus card renders its priority chip row (All / Low / Medium / High / Critical) and the four delivery cards (Sunil Joshi, Andrew McDownland, Christopher Jamil, Nirav Joshi with their budgets and priority pills) with the reference rounded pale-blue MaterialPro treatment on desktop and mobile.
On a 390px mobile viewport the dashboard has no horizontal overflow (document width stays within the viewport, tolerance 24px) on both the initial and scrolled-down dashboard states.
The filter card is present on the dashboard, the delivery tracker (/tables/basic-table) and the sample workspace (/sample-page) surfaces, using the shared shell component rather than a per-page copy.

Clicking a priority chip filters the card grid AND updates the readout to name the active priority and filtered count (e.g. clicking High yields "Showing 1 of 4 · High"), rather than freezing on the mount-time "Showing 4 of 4 · All" label.
The Basic Table route, dashboard charts, profile/contacts/activity cards, app shell and local assets continue to render with no new console errors, failed requests, or overflow.
design_constraints: Preserve MaterialPro's Material-UI design language: rounded white card surfaces, pale-blue accent chips, spacing scale, typography, promo bar, blue header, sidebar, and dashboard Grid; only the Delivery focus card's layout, chip/card styling, route coverage and readout wiring should change.
Do not remove, rename, reorder, or reword the priority chips (All / Low / Medium / High / Critical) or the four delivery rows; content stays identical across viewports and surfaces.
The filter card must stay a single logical band rendered by the shell above each surface's own content.
The readout must read the live active priority and filtered count, not a value snapshotted at mount.
No external assets, remote fonts, analytics, or network calls may be introduced; the build must stay offline-clean.
state_constraints: desktop_initial captures the operations dashboard at 1440px with the Delivery focus filter card (priority chip row All/Low/Medium/High/Critical, four delivery cards, live 'Showing N of M · <Priority>' readout) above the card Grid; no horizontal overflow.

mobile_initial captures the same dashboard at 390px; in the defective state the fixed-width no-wrap chip row / card grid forces the document wider than the screen (horizontal overflow) and the chips/cards are flat grey blocks (visual regression).
desktop_dashboard_lower and mobile_dashboard_lower capture the dashboard scrolled to the bottom (activity timeline / contacts); the mobile overflow persists in the defective state.
desktop_basic_table and mobile_basic_table capture the delivery tracker route; the reference renders the filter card there (ops-console--tracker) while the defective state omits it.
desktop_sample_page captures the sample workspace route; the reference renders the filter card there (ops-console--workspace) while the defective state omits it.
desktop_board_switch captures the dashboard after clicking the High priority chip; the reference readout flips to 'Showing 1 of 4 · High' while the defective state freezes on 'Showing 4 of 4 · All'.

Source inspection confirms the site is a Vite + TypeScript MUI dashboard whose filter-card layout/styling lives in src/components/delivery/opsConsole.styles.ts, readout wiring in src/components/delivery/opsBoardState.ts, and route coverage in src/layouts/full/FullLayout.tsx.

change_completion: The Delivery focus card no longer overflows horizontally on the 390px mobile dashboard (initial and scrolled).
Clicking a priority chip live-updates the readout to the active priority and filtered count (e.g. 'Showing 1 of 4 · High') instead of freezing on the mount-time label.
All five priority chips and the four delivery rows remain present with unchanged wording and order.
design_consistency: The repaired chips and cards use MaterialPro's rounded pale-blue accent treatment rather than flat borderless grey blocks or a collapsed dark slab.
The filter card stays a single band above each surface's content and reuses the shared shell component across routes.
regression: The delivery tracker route, dashboard charts, cards and app shell render unchanged with no new console errors or failed requests.
The filter card is present on the dashboard, tracker and workspace surfaces rather than only the dashboard.
responsive: 390px dashboard states have no horizontal overflow (tolerance 24px).
The priority chips and card grid reflow/wrap to fit narrow viewports rather than forcing a fixed-width row.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Vite+TS Material-UI admin dashboard (MaterialPro React Lite) repair/implementation_continuity/layout task, hardened to L4. Runability passes through an offline Vite build served with SPA fallback. The native lever is the Delivery focus filter card rendered by the FullLayout shell — a priority filter (All/Low/Medium/High/Critical) over the app's OWN Basic Table delivery rows with a live 'Showing N of M · <Priority>' readout, on-brand rounded pale-blue MaterialPro chips and cards, and responsive imagery. Four orthogonal defects: mobile horizontal overflow on the chip row/grid (D6), a collapsed dark-on-dark / flat-grey visual regression (D3 over the filter-card component crop), missing card on the tracker and workspace routes (D2 cross-page dom), and a stale-closure readout that freezes after a priority chip is clicked (D4 interaction). Reference passes all four; the baseline is the original-with-defect (overflow + flat-grey slab + dashboard-only card, but a live readout so it passes D4); the bad solution collapses the chips/cards into an illegible near-black slab, keeps the overflow, drops the workspace route, and freezes the readout, failing all four gates. Leg-varying source is limited to the OpsConsole styles/state and the FullLayout route map.
